Subject: Re: Redwood deployment questions (BYOK + 7yr retention + SSO audit)

Quick security triage:
- BYOK: We support CMKs via our Dedicated/Private control plane. Escrow is not our standard offering — legal/forensics requests typically route through customer KMS snapshots + formal eDiscovery warrants. Implementing an operator-managed escrow to a third-party HSM is non-trivial (key custody, dual-control, auditable copies) and will require Security & Legal sign-off. Risk: if we escrow, we expand our compliance surface.
- Rotation: We can support automatic rotation hooks but need the customer's KMS API spec (rotate/unwrap endpoints).
- Long retention: Storing PHI for 7 years increases our attack surface and retention cost. We can implement retention classes (tiered storage) but need product to define retention-scoped artifacts.
- SSO correlation: Low-risk feature. Recommend we add an optional request header capturing SAML assertion_id and user_id which we link in audit logs. Engineering impact ~3 weeks to add header plumbing + 1 week to dashboarding.

I recommend: 1) ask MediSure to narrow which artifact types require 7yr keep; 2) offer an exception flow for dev/test (shorter retention) while we scope enterprise escrow as a paid integration.

— Grace O'Connor
Head of Product Security

Reference: SEC-1392 (already on our board)

Engineering notes / rough estimate:
- SAML assertion_id pass-through: ~2 engineer-weeks to add header + audit plumbing, plus 1 week QA + dashboard work. Backwards-compatible toggle behind a runtime flag.
- Retention classes: we can tag request artifacts at write-time and route to long-term blob store. Work: storage policy + retention purge job + billing changes. Estimated 4-6 sprints if prioritized across infra and billing.
- Escrow automation: requires KMS vendor integrations (e.g., AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault) and an operator UI for escrow requests. Minimum viable integration (manual export + signed receipt) possible in ~6 weeks; fully automated, auditable escrow ~4 months and legal alignment.

Blockers: product definition of exactly which tables/blobs are in-scope; legal on escrow contract; procurement on SLA (RTO/RPO) for key recovery.

— Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
